subject: physics_2
question_text: A transformer converts 200 V a.c. into 2000 V a.c. Calculate the number of turns on the secondary if the primary has 10 turns.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: Nₛ = Vₛ Nₚ / Vₚ = 2000 × 10 / 200 = 100 turns — a step-up by 10 in voltage needs 10 times the turns, matching the book's printed answer of 100.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The turns relation
lines: For a transformer the voltage ratio equals
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the relation and the given values before any arithmetic.
steps.why: The relation Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ is the whole physics of the problem — an ideal transformer changes the voltage in exactly the ratio of its turns, so the next step is only substitution.
common_mistakes: Writing the ratio upside down, Nₛ/Nₚ = Vₚ/Vₛ. Check it: a higher secondary voltage needs more secondary turns.
Mixing up the two voltages. 200 V is the primary and 2000 V is the secondary.

recall.must_convey: That the voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ, with Vₚ = 200 V, Vₛ = 2000 V and Nₚ = 10.
accept: V s by V p equals N s by N p

steps.memory_tip: More voltage out needs more turns — voltage and turns sit on the same side of the ratio.

steps.label: Substitute and solve
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The examiner wants the substitution line and the boxed number with its unit, turns.
steps.why: Solving the ratio for Nₛ turns the physics into one line of arithmetic: 2000 × 10 / 200 = 100 turns on the secondary.
common_mistakes: Dividing the wrong way and getting Nₛ = 1 turn. A step-up from 200 V to 2000 V must multiply the turns by 10, not divide them.

recall.must_convey: That Nₛ = Vₛ Nₚ / Vₚ = 2000 × 10 / 200 = 100 turns.

steps.memory_tip: The voltage goes up ten times, so the turns go up ten times: 10 becomes 100.

insider_note: The relation line Vₛ/Vₚ = Nₛ/Nₚ carries a mark on its own — students who jump straight to 100 risk losing it.
